title: AI-Powered Personalization in Digital Banking: A Review of Customer Behavior Analytics and Engagement
authors: Ashrafuzzaman, M.; Parveen, R.; Sumiya, M. A.; Rahman, A.
tldr: A PRISMA-based systematic review of 111 peer-reviewed articles (2014-2024) finds that AI personalization in digital banking improves satisfaction and retention but faces inconsistent measurement frameworks, regulatory uncertainty, and limited cross-cultural research.
problem_and_motivation: Financial institutions increasingly deploy AI for customer personalization, yet the academic literature remains fragmented across diverse methodologies and inconsistent metrics. There is no comprehensive synthesis linking AI techniques, behavioral analytics, and engagement outcomes in digital banking.
approach: Applied the PRISMA 2020 systematic review framework to ensure methodological rigor, transparency, and reproducibility.
Searched five major academic databases in March 2025 using Boolean keyword combinations, yielding 1,248 initial records.
Removed 236 duplicates, screened 1,012 articles by title and abstract, and excluded 634 for irrelevance, leaving 378 for full-text assessment.
Excluded 267 additional articles for lacking AI personalization focus, limited banking application, or methodological shortcomings, resulting in 111 final inclusions.
Coded extracted data in Microsoft Excel by publication year, country, methodology, AI technique, personalization strategy, behavioral analytics, and engagement outcomes.

Organized findings thematically into seven domains: foundational AI techniques, behavioral analytics, personalization strategies, engagement outcomes, ethical issues, emerging-market innovations, and research gaps.
findings: num: 92 of 111 studies emphasized AI-driven personalization as integral to digital banking transformation, collectively cited over 8,500 times.
num: 81 studies identified customer behavior analytics as the primary driver of AI personalization, with approximately 6,900 cumulative citations.
num: 69 articles focused on predictive analytics for customer engagement, accumulating over 5,200 citations.
num: 74 articles addressed AI-personalization impact on satisfaction, retention, and lifetime value, with more than 7,300 cumulative citations.
num: 63 articles discussed ethical, legal, and governance challenges, cited over 6,000 times.
num: 58 articles covered AI-personalization in emerging markets, collectively cited more than 4,800 times.
num: 66 studies discussed conceptual and methodological challenges, accumulating over 5,500 citations.
Customer behavior analytics has shifted from demographic-based profiling to behavior-based classification using transaction frequency, spending patterns, and digital engagement metrics.
Reinforcement learning is gaining traction for real-time decision optimization across customer touchpoints.
Emerging markets use alternative data sources such as utility payments, mobile money activity, and airtime purchases to enable financial inclusion through AI personalization.

definitions.definition: Artificial Intelligence, the simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems.
Machine Learning, a subset of AI enabling systems to extract patterns from data without explicit programming.
Deep Learning, a multi-layered neural network approach for processing unstructured data.
Natural Language Processing, an AI technique enabling machines to interpret and generate human language.
Reinforcement Learning, a machine learning paradigm where agents learn optimal actions through reward-based feedback loops.
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, a standardized framework for systematic reviews.
Explainable AI, models designed to provide transparent and interpretable explanations for automated decisions.
Personal Finance Management, AI-powered features assisting users with budgeting, goal setting, and spending analysis.
General Data Protection Regulation, an EU legal framework governing consent, transparency, and data portability.
California Consumer Privacy Act, a US regulation establishing consumer rights over personal data collection and use.
Customer Relationship Management, platforms integrating AI for automated customer journey optimization.
Rotating Savings and Credit Associations, community-based financial products recommended through AI personalization.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review synthesizes 111 peer-reviewed articles to map the state of AI-powered personalization in digital banking across seven thematic domains.
directly_justifies: num: 92 of 111 studies confirm AI personalization is integral to digital banking transformation with over 8,500 cumulative citations.
num: 81 studies identify customer behavior analytics as the primary driver of AI personalization.
num: 66 studies document conceptual and methodological challenges including inconsistent measurement.
Banks leveraging AI for contextual and real-time personalization achieve stronger engagement and satisfaction.
Emerging markets use alternative data sources to enable financial inclusion through AI personalization.
limits: Predominantly cross-sectional and case-specific studies limit understanding of long-term AI effectiveness.
Lack of standardized metrics for measuring personalization and engagement outcomes complicates cross-study comparison.
Research heavily concentrated in Western countries with limited empirical work in Africa, South Asia, and Latin America.
Few studies integrate behavioral analytics with attitudinal outcomes such as loyalty or advocacy.
Cultural variables such as uncertainty avoidance and power distance are rarely incorporated into personalization analytical models.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned for relevance. Domain 5 was flagged as highly relevant because the paper's core focus is on behavioral data modeling for customer profiling. Domain 6 is highly relevant given extensive review of predictive analytics. Domain 10 is highly relevant as the paper dedicates substantial coverage to GDPR, CCPA, consent management, and trust. Domain 11 is highly relevant due to detailed analysis of personalization effects on satisfaction and retention.

limitations: Predominantly cross-sectional and case-specific studies limit understanding of long-term AI effectiveness.
Lack of standardized metrics for measuring personalization and engagement outcomes complicates cross-study comparison.
Research heavily concentrated in Western countries with limited empirical work in emerging markets.
Few studies integrate behavioral analytics with attitudinal outcomes such as loyalty or advocacy.
Cultural variables are rarely incorporated into personalization analytical models.
Limited discussion of how personalization outcomes differ across touchpoints or evolve over time.
Absence of time-series analysis limits understanding of feedback loops and system fatigue in AI models.
remember_this: 92 of 111 studies confirm AI personalization is integral to digital banking transformation with over 8,500 cumulative citations.
Inconsistent measurement frameworks and lack of longitudinal studies are the most persistent methodological gaps.
Behavioral analytics has replaced demographic profiling as the primary driver of customer segmentation.
Emerging markets innovate with alternative data sources and hybrid AI-human models despite infrastructure constraints.
Customer trust in AI banking depends on transparency, explainable decisions, and granular user control over personalization settings.
